script.base: Spread and total were not saved, so this script is inferred only from L3 form and season defensive rates, not from a market number. Neither defense blitzes much (TEN 22%, HOU 21%), and both QBs are worse when not blitzed (Stroud -0.03 EPA/dropback, n=34; Ward -0.17, n=30), so the lean is lower-efficiency passing rather than a shootout. Tennessee's offense runs through Pollard (47 carries, 186 yards, 3.96 YPC, about 62 rush yards a game over weeks 2-4). Houston's run game has been poor (Montgomery 2.48 YPC on 27 carries, Marks 2.37 on 19), so Houston's viable path is short and middle throws, where Schultz has 19 targets and 179 yards, not a Montgomery clock-grind. Who leads and the pace are unknown without a spread.
script.flip1: Houston blitzes well above its 21% rate. Ward's EPA vs blitz is +0.14 (n=30), Tate (26 targets, 230 yards, 312 air yards over L3) hits the explosives Houston has allowed (17 passes of 20+ on 156 attempts), Tennessee abandons the Pollard lean, and the game becomes a Tennessee pass script. Montgomery's rush under still holds; a Tate over would be a different stack and is not in this slip.
script.flip2: Tennessee blitzes well above 22%. Stroud's EPA vs blitz is +0.47 (n=34), Houston's deep air (Hutchinson 304 air yards, Noel 125, Boutte 128 over L3) actually converts, and Houston either pulls away or trades scores. Schultz's over still holds on volume. Montgomery's under fails only if that lead turns into a clock-grind of 12+ carries rather than more throws.

Montgomery does not overlap a weak run fit for an over: even at TEN's 3.88 YPC, his L3 pace of 9 carries is about 35 yards. Tate (312 air yards) would overlap HOU's explosive allowance, but alignment is missing and that overlap needs the blitz flip, so it is not the leg.

data_check.notes: No projection, sim median, or Pinnacle no-vig is in the pack, so this check is L3 form and season defensive rates against the listed lines only. Montgomery 67 yards on 27 carries is 22.3 per game versus 43.5; 9 carries times TEN 3.88 YPC allowed is 34.9, still under, and 11 carries at 3.88 is 42.7. Schultz 179 yards over 3 games is 59.7 versus 34.0. TEN middle 8.21 YPA on 24 attempts supports the area rather than opposing it. Stroud's no-blitz EPA of -0.03 and TEN's 22% blitz rate are already in the script as a volume risk, not a contradiction of the recorded 179 yards. TEN's 11 runs of 10+ cap how hard the Montgomery under can be; they do not put 9 carries over 43.5.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost because the missing spread hid a Houston lead: Houston ground the clock, Montgomery got 14 carries, and one of the 10-plus yard runs Tennessee has already allowed 11 of this season pushed him through 43.5 even without a true efficiency fix. Schultz lost the same script from the other side, or lost a slog in which Tennessee stayed at a 22% blitz, Stroud sat on his -0.03 no-blitz EPA, and the 20 Houston targets Hutchinson has drawn (304 air yards, only 134 yards) plus Noel and Boutte ate the volume so Schultz finished on 4 targets around 25 yards. A late inactive not in this pack would void either leg. The counter is real on script because the spread is missing, but it is not stronger than 27 carries at 2.48 YPC versus 43.5, so the Montgomery under stays and Schultz stays a lean rather than a strong.
slip_story: One story only: Houston's run game stays broken and the offense's answer is Schultz in the short and middle, not a shootout and not a favorite clock-grind. Stack is Montgomery rush yards under 43.5 with Schultz rec yards over 34. Do not add Hutchinson, Noel, Boutte, or Tate overs, a game total over, or Collins either side; those need the blitz flip, a role the pack does not confirm, or a total that was not saved. Do not add Marks under in the same slip without an inactive list, because a Montgomery scratch redistributes the carries. Pre-kickoff log only.
